title: Shining Wisdom
subtitle: A squire in Odegan
summary: Shining Wisdom is Sonic! Software Planning and Camelot's action adventure, first released for Saturn in Japan on 11 August 1995.
body: Shining Wisdom is Sonic! Software Planning and Camelot's action adventure, first released for Saturn in Japan on 11 August 1995. The player controls Mars, a young squire in Odegan who becomes involved in the dark elf Pazort's plans against the kingdom. The story follows a single adventurer through an overhead world of enemies and puzzles. Sword attacks and movement take place directly in that world, giving this Shining game a different rhythm from the party-based battles associated with much of the series. Progress comes through exploration and the useful equipment found along the way.

Mars uses combinations of acquired items and magical orbs to expand what he can do. Choosing that equipment matters to both combat and obstacles, giving the player a reason to reconsider a route after finding something new. His attacks depend on direct control and movement rather than a party's turn-based commands. The large world places puzzles between its confrontations, so knowing where an ability can be applied becomes part of navigation. A new item can make an earlier obstruction into a useful destination, connecting collection with a concrete change in the journey.

The project began as a Mega Drive game before being adapted for Saturn, retaining a two-dimensional structure with pre-rendered character sprites. Its story also connects to Shining Force II through the setting of Parmecia and returning characters, although changes in the North American translation obscured those links. Motoaki Takenouchi composed the music. Shining Wisdom shows how broadly the series could interpret an adventure: the continuing fictional world remained, while the player's attention moved towards one character's speed, equipment and ability to solve a passage directly.
